1.title: The Organizing Practice
1.text: Welcome to Module six: The Organizing Practice. It covers the exam area The prince two practices. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Explain the purpose of the organizing practice and its relationships with the principles. Explain the purpose of the project management team structure, role descriptions and commercial management approach. Define project board and project team. Describe the three project interests, the prince two roles and the work breakdown structure. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The prince two practices (sixty percent). Exam format: sixty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; thirty-six correct answers (sixty percent) pass. Validated against: the official prince two seven Foundation syllabus (people cert).

1.title: Purpose
1.text: Purpose. The organizing practice defines the accountability structure of the project: who is responsible for what, and how everyone works together. It supports the principle define roles, responsibilities and relationships.

1.title: The three project interests
1.text: The three project interests. Every project must represent three interests. Business. The Executive (is the project worthwhile and good value?). User. The Senior User(s) (will the products meet the need?). Supplier. The Senior Supplier(s) (can the products be delivered as specified?).

1.title: The project board and the project team
1.text: The project board and the project team. Project board. The group accountable for the project's success: Executive, Senior User(s) and Senior Supplier(s). Project team. The people who manage and deliver the project day to day: the project manager, team managers and team members (with support).

1.title: The project board and the project team, continued
1.text: The project board and the project team. The figure shows this: The project management team: directing, managing and delivering levels.

1.title: The PRINCE2 roles
1.text: The prince two roles. Executive. Ultimately accountable for the project; owns the business case; chairs the board. Senior User. Specifies the needs of users and ensures the products meet them. Senior Supplier. Represents the suppliers; accountable for the quality of what is delivered by the supplier side. Project manager. Day-to-day management within the tolerances set by the board. Team manager. Delivers the products for the project manager (optional role). Project assurance. Independent checks on behalf of the business, user and supplier interests. Change authority. Has delegated authority to approve or reject changes. Project support. Administrative help (planning tools, filing, reporting). Exam tip: The board is accountable; the project manager manages; the team manager delivers. Project assurance should be independent of the project manager.

1.title: The work breakdown structure
1.text: The work breakdown structure. A work breakdown structure (W B S) is a hierarchical breakdown of the total work needed to deliver the project's products, down to manageable pieces that can be assigned and estimated. It shows who does what and supports planning and control.

1.title: Management products
1.text: Management products. Project management team structure (P I D). The roles and reporting lines of the project. Role descriptions (P I D). What each role is responsible for. Commercial management approach (P I D). How the project manages suppliers and contracts. Exam tip: The Executive is the single point of accountability for the project. Do not confuse the Executive with the project manager, who works within tolerances. Exam tip: Project assurance is independent: the person who manages the project does not assure it.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Who is ultimately accountable for the success of the project? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: The Executive. The Executive is ultimately accountable.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which statements about the project board are C O R R E C T? (one) It is accountable for the project's success. (two) It includes the Executive, Senior User and Senior Supplier. (three) It manages the project day to day. (four) It is made up only of team managers. The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: one and two. The board is accountable and has those three roles.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Identify the missing word. The blank role represents the user interest and specifies user needs. The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Senior User. That is the Senior User.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which role delivers the products for the project manager? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Team manager. Team managers deliver the products.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A group has delegated authority to approve or reject changes. Which role is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Change authority. The change authority decides on changes within its delegated authority.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. What is a work breakdown structure? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A hierarchical breakdown of the total work to be done. It breaks the total work into manageable pieces.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Name the three project interests. Answer: Business, user and supplier. Question two. Who makes up the project board? Answer: The Executive, Senior User(s) and Senior Supplier(s). Question three. What does project assurance do? Answer: Independent checks on the business, user and supplier interests.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the project manager's authority limited by? Answer: The tolerances set by the project board. Question five. Which P I D product describes how suppliers and contracts are handled? Answer: The commercial management approach. Question six. What does a role description state? Answer: What each role is responsible for.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Interests: business (Executive), user (Senior User), supplier (Senior Supplier). Board: accountable; Executive plus Senior User plus Senior Supplier. Team: project manager, team managers, team members, support. Other roles: project assurance (independent), change authority, project support. Products: team structure, role descriptions, commercial management approach.
